abstract: Embryonal carcinoma cells (EC cells) can form a wide variety of differentiated cell types and thus resemble the pluripotential stem cells of the normal embryo. Certain EC cell derivatives acquire the biochemical and morphological features of primitive endoderm and have been called 'END' or endodermlike cells. Although these have also been called 'giant' because of their large size, their nuclear DNA contents are not known. Since cell size often corresponds to DNA content and primitive endoderm becomes polyploid during the course of normal development, EC-derived endoderm has been studied cytophotometrically. Thus, EC- and embryo-derived endoderm were found to be similar in that both of these tissues undergo polyploidization. Moreover, the polyploid cells of either EC or embryonic origin do not appear to be terminal cell types, since they can occasionally enter renewed cell division in spite of their large size.
abstract_ja: 胎児性癌(EC)細胞は多様な分化細胞型を形成でき、正常胚の多能性幹細胞に類似する。EC細胞由来の一部の細胞は原始内胚葉の生化学的および形態学的特徴を獲得し、「END」または内胚葉様細胞と呼ばれてきた。これらは大型であることから「巨大」細胞とも呼ばれてきたが、核DNA含量は知られていなかった。細胞サイズはしばしばDNA含量と相関し、原始内胚葉は正常発生の過程で倍数化するため、EC由来の内胚葉を細胞計測法により解析した。その結果、EC由来の内胚葉と胚由来の内胚葉はいずれも倍数化するという点で類似していることがわかった。さらに、ECまたは胚由来の倍数性細胞は終末分化細胞ではなく、大型であるにもかかわらず時折再び細胞分裂に入ることができる。
